cases.description: Microsoft's first documented example, which the page prints in scientific notation
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes =SECH(45) = 5.73E-20. DERIVATION: 1/cosh(45 rad) = 5.72503716109878728894e-20 at 50 digits (mpmath), which is 5.73E-20 at the three significant figures the page prints. Asserted here at 25 decimal places -- ROUND(x,25) lands on 5.72504e-20 -- so the assertion carries THREE more significant digits than the page's 5.73E-20 while claiming nothing the derivation does not have. Same description/unit error as SEC: the page calls it "the hyperbolic secant of a 45 degree angle" while its own Remarks say to convert degrees with PI()/180, and 45 radians is what reproduces the published figure. Microsoft's page was read live on 2026-08-31 at https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/functions/sech-function. FETCH NOTE FOR THIS BATCH: batch F recorded every /en-us/office/<name>-function-<guid> URL returning Microsoft's 'Sorry, the page you're looking for can't be found' body; today BOTH paths serve the article again -- the GUID form redirects to /en-us/excel/functions/<slug>-function -- and every page cited in this batch came back complete (217-223 KB) in one or two attempts, with no 87 KB stub responses. Nothing here is sourced from a search snippet or a mirror.

Microsoft publishes =SECH(30) = 1.87E-13. Derived independently as 1/cosh(30 rad) = 1.871524593768034920983e-13, i.e. 1.87E-13 at the published three significant figures. Rounded here to 20 decimals, which lands on 1.8715246e-13 -- five more significant digits than the page prints -- for the same reason as the 45 case.

cases.description: A structural identity with no derived constant: sech(0) = 1 exactly
cases.expected_note: cosh(0) = 1 exactly, so sech(0) = 1 exactly. No rounding, no published figure, nothing to get wrong except the function itself -- a sharp check that the engine computes a hyperbolic secant rather than a circular one (cos(0) is also 1, so this case does NOT distinguish them; the 45 and 30 cases, whose circular and hyperbolic values differ by nineteen orders of magnitude, do).

cases.description: sech is an even function, so a sign flip must change nothing
cases.expected_note: cosh is even, so sech is even and sech(2) - sech(-2) = 0 exactly. A structural assertion with no derived constant. NOTE ON READ-BACK: a formula returning 0 round-trips through .xlsx normally here (it is a genuine numeric zero, not a blank), unlike the empty-string case documented in RIGHTB.json.

cases.description: A non-numeric argument, which the page assigns an error code
cases.expected_note: The Remarks publish: "If number is a nonnumeric value, SECH returns the #VALUE! error values." (Microsoft's plural, as published).

cases.description: An argument beyond the documented magnitude limit
cases.expected_note: The Remarks publish the same constraint SEC carries: "The absolute value of number must be less than 2^27" (= 134217728) and "If number is outside its constraints, SECH returns the #NUM! error value." LIBREOFFICE DOES NOT ENFORCE THE LIMIT: all four builds returned 0 rather than #NUM!. That is a silent wrong answer rather than a harmless permissiveness, and the limit exists precisely because of it -- at 2e8 radians the argument reduction consumes every bit of a double's precision, so the hyperbolic secant simply underflows to zero. Excel documents the guard; LibreOffice computes through it.
